command:
git fetch -q --tags origin; echo -n 'refs matching v0.8.2 exactly: '; git ls-remote --tags origin 'refs/tags/v0.8.2' | wc -l | tr -d ' '; echo -n 'existing v0.8.* tags: '; git ls-remote --tags origin 'v0.8.*' | grep -v '\^{}' | awk '{print $2}' | tr '
' ' '
note: The gate is named for 0.8.0 because it was written for that checklist; what it checks here is that this release's own tag does not already exist. The v0.8.2rc tags are the D-0216 rehearsal cuts: rc1 and rc2 were stopped in prepare before anything was uploaded, and rc3 ran green end to end and is published as a pre-release. Matched exactly, not by prefix, so a rehearsal tag cannot stand in for the release tag.
result: no ref on origin matches refs/tags/v0.8.2; origin carries refs/tags/v0.8.0, refs/tags/v0.8.1 and the three rehearsal tags refs/tags/v0.8.2rc1, refs/tags/v0.8.2rc2 and refs/tags/v0.8.2rc3
